name: com.midmanstudio.dragndrop
description: Framework-agnostic drag-and-drop core: a single DragDropController state machine that a uGUI adapter or a UI Toolkit adapter feeds identically, so unrelated systems (inventory slots, the chemistry bench's reagent tray, HudMan's HUD layout editor, anything else) can share one drag interaction layer without depending on each other. Zero game-specific logic, and the Core assembly stays deliberately zero-.mdix and zero-UnityEngine dependent -- there's no static catalog to drive here, just runtime interaction state. 0.2.0 added the first concrete adapter: Runtime/UGUI, a small uGUI/EventSystems layer (DragDropControllerHost, UGuiDraggableSource, UGuiDropTargetZone) that any RectTransform-based UI can drop onto without hand-rolling IBeginDragHandler/IDragHandler/IEndDragHandler again. 0.3.0 adds the UI Toolkit adapter: Runtime/UIToolkit (UIToolkitDraggableSource, UIToolkitDropTargetZone), built on real PointerDownEvent/PointerMoveEvent/PointerUpEvent/PointerEnterEvent/PointerLeaveEvent/PointerCaptureOutEvent + PointerCaptureHelper, using style.left/style.top on an absolutely-positioned element for drag positioning. Deliberately plain C# rather than MonoBehaviours -- a VisualElement has no GameObject/sibling-component concept, so both classes take the VisualElement, the IDraggable/IDropTarget, and the shared DragDropController directly in their constructor instead of resolving one via a GameObject-hierarchy host the way the uGUI adapter's DragDropControllerHost does; UI Toolkit UIs are built in code by a presenter that already owns the controller, so there's no hierarchy to walk and nothing to resolve. This assembly references only MidManStudio.DragDrop.Runtime -- it has no dependency on the UGUI assembly or vice versa, matching the Core's own doc comment that neither adapter needs to know the other exists.
